### I use population and behavioral data to understand why outcomes differ across people and places.

I'm a quantitative researcher trained in epidemiology. Across different topics and settings, I've stayed interested in the same challenge of figuring out what imperfect data can tell us about the world.

[More about me →](about.qmd)

\

## How I Work

**Start with the problem.**\
Sometimes the question is already clear. Sometimes part of the work is figuring out what question should be asked in the first place. Either way, I start by understanding what decision the analysis is meant to inform.

**Interrogate the data.**\
Before running any models, I spend time understanding where the data came from and what assumptions are built into it. Most analytical errors happen here.

**Choose methods that fit.**\
Some questions require causal methods. Others are better answered with segmentation, descriptive analysis, or a well-made chart. I care more about fit than sophistication.

**Interpret the evidence.**\
Results rarely speak for themselves. Part of the job is translating findings into language that supports clear decisions, while being transparent about what the data can and cannot support.
